title: Two scheduled workflows turned main red every hour and every morning, for a billing reason no code change could fix, and reported it only in an annotation
detected_by: the session resolving CI, reading the annotation endpoint after `gh run view --log-failed` answered `log not found`

first_order.what_broke: ci-fleet-keeper (hourly, cron 17 * * * *) and ci-fleet-watch (daily, cron 30 6 * * *) both target `runs-on: ubuntu-latest`. This account cannot start a GitHub-hosted job at all, so both jobs conclude `failure` having run ZERO steps. main was therefore red once an hour and once every morning, on two checks that had nothing to do with any diff.
first_order.receipt: Run 32343624520, job 96347602802: {"conclusion":"failure","started_at":"2026-08-20T07:21:24Z","completed_at":"2026-08-20T07:21:27Z","steps":0}. `gh run view --log-failed` answers `log not found: 96371203101`. The only record anywhere is the check-run annotation, verbatim: "The job was not started because recent account payments have failed or your spending limit needs to be increased. Please check the 'Billing & plans' section in your settings". Read it with `gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/check-runs/<job_id>/annotations`.
first_order.fixed_by: Both jobs now carry `if: vars.HOSTED_RUNNERS_AVAILABLE == 'yes'`, so they SKIP instead of failing. Turning them back on after billing is fixed is `gh variable set HOSTED_RUNNERS_AVAILABLE --body yes` and needs no code change. Pinned by tests/unit/test_ci_fleet_keeper.py::test_the_keeper_is_skipped_and_not_failed_while_hosted_runners_cannot_start and tests/unit/test_ci_fleet_probe.py::test_the_watch_is_skipped_and_not_failed_while_hosted_runners_cannot_start; both were mutation-proved against origin/main's copy of the workflow, where jobs.watch.if is None and the assertion fails.

cause_chain: main went red on a schedule -> the failing job ran zero steps -> its log 404s, so the usual instrument returns nothing -> the reason lives only in a check-run annotation -> the reason is that account payments failed, which is a founder decision and not a code defect -> a check that is red every morning for a reason nobody in CI can act on is a check that trains the estate to ignore red.

second_order.premise_refuted: ci-fleet-keeper's own header argued that the Free plan's 2,000 GitHub-hosted minutes are an emergency reserve for ci.yml, whose runner label falls back to `|| 'ubuntu-latest'` when the CI_*_RUNS_ON variables are unset. That reserve does not exist. The fallback is an instant no-steps failure, which reads as nothing at all. If the fly pool ever goes down, ci.yml has no escape hatch.
second_order.why_not_moved_to_the_fleet: Neither job was moved to the `fly` pool, and that is deliberate in both cases. A self-hosted runner cannot start a dead self-hosted fleet, because when the fleet is down there is no runner left to pick the job up. And a fleet running the wrong image cannot be trusted to report that it is running the wrong image. Skipping loses the check; moving it would keep a check that lies.
second_order.cost_of_the_skip: While the switch is off, the fleet has no self-heal and the image-staleness question goes unasked. Both are answered by hand: `.venv/bin/python scripts/ci_fleet_keeper.py --start` and `.venv/bin/python scripts/ci_fleet_probe.py --image-only`, and both are ops console buttons.

third_order.silence: A skipped job is silent, and silence is what this estate keeps reading as health. ci-fleet-keeper gained an `announce` job that runs on the fly pool whenever the switch is off, states the outage and the annotation in the step summary, and SUCCEEDS. So the hourly tick is a green run carrying a reason instead of a red run carrying a message only the founder can act on. ci-fleet-watch adds no second alarm on purpose: one announcement an hour is enough, and two would be the same noise twice.

grade.class: a failure mode whose only record is outside the instrument everyone uses. A job that never starts has no log, so every habit built on `gh run view --log-failed` reports nothing and the run looks unexplained rather than explained.
grade.self_healing: not possible — the cause is a payment, which is the founder's alone
grade.guard: two tests pin the `if:` gate as an exact string in both workflows, so deleting the gate without deciding to is a red suite rather than an hourly red main
grade.memory: the annotation endpoint as the source of truth for a zero-step job is already recorded in memory `a-killed-runner-reads-as-a-failing-test.md`; this incident is its second instance with a different cause
grade.founder_action: fix Actions billing, then `gh variable set HOSTED_RUNNERS_AVAILABLE --body yes`
